result.title: Where Does the Performance Go? Understanding and Recovering Performance Regressions in C-to-Rust Translation
result.summary: Rust is increasingly adopted as a memory-safe successor to C, and transpilers such as \crust{} can migrate entire C projects while preserving their behavior. Preserving behavior, however, does not guarantee preserving performance. We study this gap on 20 real-world C projects and their \crust{} translations. On the eight projects used for analysis, the translated Rust is more than 3\% slower than the original C on 12 of 19 operations, by up to 62.2\%. By comparing execution-cost profiles, optimized LLVM IR, and compiler optimization remarks across each C--Rust pair, we trace these slowdowns to nine recurring performance issues, spanning residual runtime work, missed compiler optimizations, and C-style source patterns, and derive an optimization direction for each. We then present \ourtool{}, an LLM-based approach that encodes these issues as reusable optimization rules to recover the performance of translated Rust. \ourtool{} profiles each project to locate hot functions and matches them against rule-specific patterns. The LLM then checks each rule's rewrite preconditions against the project context before rewriting, and a rewrite is kept only if it passes both functional and performance validation. On 41 operations from twelve held-out projects, \ourtool{} preserves C outputs on all tested workloads and speeds up 40 operations over the \crust{} translations, 18 of which end up faster than the original C. It outperforms the general-purpose coding agent \codex{} on 31 of the 37 operations where both preserve C outputs, and outperforms its own variant without rule guidance on 34 of the 41 operations.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 C 到 Rust 转译中的性能回退问题：通过对比执行开销画像、优化后 LLVM IR 与编译器优化报告，归纳出九类重复出现的慢化原因，并据此用规则引导的 LLM 重写热点函数，仅在通过功能与性能双重验证时保留改写。
AI.relevance_reason: 对象是 C-to-Rust 代码转译的性能归因与 LLM 重写，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据筛选或 latent 生成；其「画像定位热点＋规则前置条件＋验证保留」属通用代码优化流程，未提供可供核查的 LVR 借鉴线索，故排除。
